clinician.final_diagnosis: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with metastatic pituitary lesion
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and HIV presented with headache, neurological symptoms including left then bilateral ptosis and ophthalmoplegia, and systemic symptoms. MRI abdomen revealed a large hepatic lesion (8.7×8.5 cm) in the right posterior hepatic lobe suspicious for HCC (E005). Clinical progression included worsening neurological deficits (E006), and head CT showed a pituitary mass invading the cavernous sinus (E007). Although histopathology reports with safe excerpts were not provided, the known final diagnosis confirms liver biopsy results consistent with HCC and transsphenoidal pituitary biopsy confirming metastatic HCC.
